The selective sources change the baseline and lead to a stronger construction. **N1511 already earns the interacting common-loss first-event receiver, and N1512 already earns its near-linear activity schedule with actual controlled-duration accounting.** Their accepted internal reviews are preserved at their actual scope. My second-stage comparison omitted these results; the frozen report is unchanged and this return corrects that omission.

The new result is a constructive extension to a checked class of **coupled, nonnormal Gaussian memories with unequal or rank-deficient loss**. It earns a time-uniform occupation bound, an actual linear-activity emitted-count cap, a bounded-filter no-jump source using the acquired Dots scalar bridge, and an exponentially weighted physical loss clock. The complete resource envelope is near-linear in extensive activity and ordinary system action after explicit metric, mode, cutoff and precision factors. This is author-derived and still awaits independent review of the whole new conjunction.

    V=sum_j Q_j(c_j b+b^dagger c_j^dagger),

with initial retained vacuum, arbitrary bounded noncommuting system operators supplied by actual circuits, arbitrary system/reference inputs, and prescribed system-only instruments with retained records. The bath and Markov output field remain private. No reset of the retained bath is introduced.

    P>=I,       A^dagger P+PA<=-gamma P,       gamma>0.

It is checked from the actual classical matrices, with its precision, slack and conditioning paid. Define

    Lambda=4a_P a_inv/gamma,
    pmax>=||P||.

The constants are not presumed favorable. Rank deficiency of EE^dagger is allowed because Hamiltonian mixing can supply decay in this metric. # A Gaussian Lyapunov lift beyond common loss

Author-derived stage-three construction, prompted by the accepted N1511/N1512 sources. Their common-loss occupation/activity/scheduling results are prior premises at their actual scope. This argument does not import their source oracle or assume that common loss applies to a rank-deficient matrix. The stage-two construction and both frozen returns are unchanged.

## 1. Input and certificate

Retain the stage-two input

    A=-iH-EE^dagger/2,
    L_mu=e_mu^dagger b,
    V=sum_j Q_j[a(c_j)+a(c_j)^dagger],
    a(c)=c b,

where the Q_j are bounded Hermitian system operators, with actual supplied block normalizations q_j. The joint system may be noncommuting and reference-entangled. The retained bath is initially vacuum. Prescribed system-only instruments and their unconditional records remain allowed.

Acquire an explicit positive Hermitian one-particle matrix P and a number gamma>0 such that

    P>=I,             A^dagger P+PA <= -gamma P.             (1)

This is an additional **checked small-matrix certificate**, not an assumed occupation theorem. Its entries, finite arithmetic, inequality slack and any conditioning are charged. Define

    a_P=sum_j q_j ||c_j P^(1/2)||,
    a_inv=sum_j q_j ||c_j P^(-1/2)||,
    mu=4 a_P^2/gamma^2,
    Lambda=4 a_P a_inv/gamma.                              (2)

These may be unfavorable and remain explicit in the cost. A Hurwitz matrix has a positive Lyapunov solution, but merely invoking that fact does not supply bounded mu or Lambda. Exact dark modes do not satisfy (1). The general stage-two theorem remains applicable without (1).

The key point is that EE^dagger itself need not be positive definite. Hamiltonian mixing can make (1) hold with bounded P and gamma even when loss has rank one and its largest rate diverges.

# Bounded metric filtering and an exponentially weighted loss clock

This strengthens the first stage-three metric consequence. It removes the linear-in-drive window penalty of the stage-two Dyson source as well as its quadratic-horizon occupation/count budgets. It receives the **actual acquired scalar immigration-death bridge** from N1511/N1512 at its positive-rate scalar interface. It does not receive their common-loss physical model for a different loss matrix. All new interface changes and the new weighted physical clock are derived below. This remains author-derived and awaits independent whole review.

## 1. An inexpensive bounded filter exposes a scalar decay

Receive the checked one-particle certificate

    P>=I,      A^dagger P+PA<=-gamma P,

and the proved metric occupation/activity bounds in `METRIC_OCCUPATION_AND_ACTIVITY.md`. Select the actual global cutoff K>=1 from that theorem. Let pmax>=||P|| be a certified finite scalar bound and define

    Z=I+P/(K pmax),
    kappa=gamma/(2K pmax),
    S=Gamma(Z^(1/2)),
    Atilde=Z^(1/2) A Z^(-1/2),
    C=Atilde+(kappa/2)I.                                  (1)

Because A+A^dagger<=0,

    A^dagger Z+ZA
       <=-gamma P/(K pmax)<=-kappa Z.

The second inequality uses P>=I and Z<=2I. Thus C+C^dagger<=0. It need not be diagonal or normal. Its forward second-quantized exponential is an explicitly acquired contraction, by the same finite-matrix Julia block construction as stage two.

On N<=K,

    ||S||<sqrt(e)<2,          ||S^(-1)||<=1.               (2)

This is the reason for using Z close to I rather than directly filtering by P. Direct use of Gamma(P^(1/2)) could cost ||P||^(K/2), which would destroy the inverse-accuracy claim. The bounded filter pays a weaker decay kappa, polynomially in K and pmax, while retaining constant filter normalization.

The filters are actual finite circuits. Diagonalize the small positive matrix Z to an absolute error allocated to K; approximate Jacobi/Givens arithmetic requires no eigenvector-gap promise.
